source_refs.note: Exercise 13.1, Question 3 (book page 248, PDF 253); answer key PDF 310-311. Printed '3.' twice; as the key, 3(i) = first, 3(ii) = second.

blocks.prompt: 3 (i) [printed as question 3] Find the derivative of \(x^{2/3}\) at \(x = 8\) from the first principle.
blocks.explanation:
Kitab mein do sawal "3." number ke saath chhape hain; answer key ki tarah hum is pehle wale ko 3(i) kehte hain.
Yeh sawal mushkil lagta hai kyunke power fraction hai: \(x^{2/3}\). Binomial ya rationalising seedha kaam nahi karte.
Plan: cube root ko naya naam denge: \(u = (x + \delta x)^{1/3}\) aur \(v = x^{1/3}\). Phir upar "difference of squares" aur neeche "difference of cubes" ban jayega, aur \(u - v\) cancel ho jayega. Aakhir mein \(x = 8\).
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(f(x) = x^{2/3}\), point \(x = 8\).
Find karna hai: \(f'(8)\), first principles se.
Tareeqa: definition (first principles / ab-initio, yani bilkul shuru se) se derivative: \(f'(x) = \lim_{\delta x \to 0} \frac{f(x + \delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x}\). Chaar steps yaad rakhein: (I) \(f(x + \delta x)\) likhein; (II) us mein se \(f(x)\) minus karein; (III) \(\delta x\) se divide karein; (IV) \(\delta x \to 0\) ka limit lein. Yeh tareeqa is liye ke Exercise 13.1 mein sawal khud 'by definition' maangta hai, aur power rule waghera abhi Section 13.6 mein aaenge; is liye shortcut nahi, poora limit ka safar dikhana hai. Naye naam: \(u = (x + \delta x)^{1/3}\), \(v = x^{1/3}\), taake \(u^3 - v^3 = \delta x\) ho jaye.

Step I aur II, \(u\) aur \(v\) mein
\[f(x + \delta x) - f(x) = (x + \delta x)^{2/3} - x^{2/3}\]
\[= u^2 - v^2\]
\[\delta x = (x + \delta x) - x = u^3 - v^3\]
Kyun: \((x + \delta x)^{2/3}\) cube root ka square hai, yani \(u^2\). Isi tarah \(x^{2/3} = v^2\). Aur \(u^3 = x + \delta x\), \(v^3 = x\), is liye \(\delta x = u^3 - v^3\). Ab saari powers whole numbers ban gayin jin ke factors hum jaante hain.

Step III: \(\delta x\) se divide aur factorise
\[\dfrac{f(x + \delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x} = \dfrac{u^2 - v^2}{u^3 - v^3}\]
\[= \dfrac{(u - v)(u + v)}{(u - v)(u^2 + uv + v^2)}\]
\[= \dfrac{u + v}{u^2 + uv + v^2}\]
Kyun: Upar difference of squares: \(u^2 - v^2 = (u - v)(u + v)\). Neeche difference of cubes: \(u^3 - v^3 = (u - v)(u^2 + uv + v^2)\). Dono mein \((u - v)\) hai. Jab tak \(\delta x \neq 0\), \(u \neq v\), is liye \((u - v)\) cancel karna jaiz hai. Yehi cancel asal mein \(\delta x\) wala cancel hai, bas naye libaas mein.

Step IV: limit lein
\[\delta x \to 0 \Rightarrow u \to v\]
\[f'(x) = \dfrac{v + v}{v^2 + v^2 + v^2} = \dfrac{2v}{3v^2}\]
\[= \dfrac{2}{3v} = \dfrac{2}{3x^{1/3}}\]
Kyun: Jab \(\delta x \to 0\), to \(x + \delta x \to x\), is liye \(u \to v\). Har \(u\) ki jagah \(v\) rakha: upar \(2v\), neeche \(3v^2\). Ek \(v\) cancel kar ke \(\frac{2}{3v}\) bacha, aur \(v = x^{1/3}\).

\(x = 8\) par value
\[f'(8) = \dfrac{2}{3 \cdot 8^{1/3}}\]
\[= \dfrac{2}{3 \cdot 2} = \dfrac{1}{3}\]
Kyun: \(8^{1/3}\) ka matlab woh number jis ka cube \(8\) ho, yani \(2\). Is liye \(f'(8) = \frac{2}{6} = \frac{1}{3}\). Yeh answer key ke \(\frac{1}{3}\) se milta hai.

Tasdeeq: Section 13.6 ke power rule se (sirf jawab confirm karne ke liye, tareeqa nahi)
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}x^{2/3} = \tfrac{2}{3}x^{-1/3}\]
\[x = 8:\ \tfrac{2}{3} \cdot \tfrac{1}{2} = \tfrac{1}{3} \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Power rule (jo rational \(n\) ke liye bhi sahi hai, Section 13.4) se bhi \(\frac{1}{3}\) aaya. Is liye hamara first-principle wala jawab pakka hai.

blocks.prompt: 3 (ii) [printed as a second question 3] Find the derivative of \(x^2 + 2x + 3\) by definition.
blocks.explanation:
Yeh kitab ka doosra "3." hai, jise answer key 3(ii) kehti hai.
Yeh Question 1(i) jaisa hi polynomial hai: definition se derivative.
Plan: wohi chaar steps. Is dafa teen terms hain, is liye har term ka \(\delta x\) wala hissa dhyan se likhna hai.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(f(x) = x^2 + 2x + 3\).
Find karna hai: \(f'(x)\), definition se.
Tareeqa: definition (first principles / ab-initio, yani bilkul shuru se) se derivative: \(f'(x) = \lim_{\delta x \to 0} \frac{f(x + \delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x}\). Chaar steps yaad rakhein: (I) \(f(x + \delta x)\) likhein; (II) us mein se \(f(x)\) minus karein; (III) \(\delta x\) se divide karein; (IV) \(\delta x \to 0\) ka limit lein. Yeh tareeqa is liye ke Exercise 13.1 mein sawal khud 'by definition' maangta hai, aur power rule waghera abhi Section 13.6 mein aaenge; is liye shortcut nahi, poora limit ka safar dikhana hai.

Step I: \(f(x + \delta x)\) nikalein
\[f(x + \delta x) = (x + \delta x)^2 + 2(x + \delta x) + 3\]
\[= x^2 + 2x\,\delta x + (\delta x)^2 + 2x + 2\,\delta x + 3\]
Kyun: Har \(x\) ki jagah \(x + \delta x\) rakha aur brackets khole. Constant \(3\) mein \(x\) hai hi nahi, is liye woh waisa hi rehta hai.

Step II: \(f(x)\) minus karein
\[f(x + \delta x) - f(x) = 2x\,\delta x + (\delta x)^2 + 2\,\delta x\]
Kyun: \(x^2\), \(2x\) aur \(3\) dono taraf hain is liye cancel. Constant \(3\) yahan gaayab ho gaya; isi liye constant ka derivative zero hota hai.

Step III: \(\delta x\) se divide karein
\[\dfrac{f(x + \delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x}\]
\[= 2x + \delta x + 2\]
Kyun: Har term se ek \(\delta x\) cancel; \(\delta x\) abhi zero nahi hai.

Step IV: limit lein
\[f'(x) = \lim_{\delta x \to 0}(2x + \delta x + 2)\]
\[= 2x + 2\]
Kyun: Koi denominator nahi bacha, is liye \(\delta x = 0\) rakh diya.

Tasdeeq: Section 13.6 ke power rule se (sirf jawab confirm karne ke liye, tareeqa nahi)
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^2 + 2x + 3) = 2x + 2 + 0 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Rule se bhi wohi jawab, aur answer key bhi \(2x + 2\) deti hai.
